author: W. W. Prescott
text: Man was created in the image of God; all have sinned, have lost the image of God, and have the earthly image; it is the purpose of God to restore that lost image.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Seth … resembled Adam more closely than did his other sons. He was a worthy character, following in the steps of Abel. Yet he inherited no more natural goodness than did Cain. … While Adam was created sinless, in the likeness of God, Seth, like Cain, inherited the fallen nature of his parents.

author: Ellen G. White
text: through disobedience, his powers were perverted, and selfishness took the place of love.

author: Ellen G. White
text: they are not punished for the parents’ guilt, except as they participate in their sins. … By inheritance and example the sons become partakers of the father’s sin.

author: Ellen G. White
text: To sin, wherever found, “our God is a consuming fire.” … if men cling to sin, they become identified with it. Then the glory of God, which destroys sin, must destroy them. … The light of the glory of God, which imparts life to the righteous, will slay the wicked.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Thoughts from the Mount of Blessing
text: If you choose sin, and refuse to separate from it, the presence of God, which consumes sin, must consume you.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Thoughts from the Mount of Blessing
text: God is the fountain of life, and we can have life only as we are in communion with Him. Separated from God, existence may be ours for a little time, but we do not possess life.

author: Ellen G. White
text: As they witnessed in drooping flower and falling leaf the first signs of decay, Adam and his companion mourned more deeply than men now mourn over their dead.

author: Ellen G. White
text: after man’s fall, holy angels were immediately commissioned to guard the tree of life. … hence there is not an immortal sinner.

author: Ellen G. White
text: His nature became so weakened through transgression that it was impossible for him, in his own strength, to resist the power of evil. He was made captive by Satan

author: Ellen G. White
text: It is impossible for us, of ourselves, to escape from the pit of sin in which we are sunken. Our hearts are evil, and we cannot change them.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: Sin binds its victims. … therefore the bondage is that of a law-breaker.

author: Ellen G. White
text: At the cherubim-guarded gate of Paradise the divine glory was revealed. Hither came Adam and his sons to worship God.

author: Ellen G. White
text: But he received also the knowledge of the Redeemer and instruction in righteousness.

author: Ellen G. White
text: As related to the first Adam, men receive from him nothing but guilt and the sentence of death.
